speaker: ivy
lines: Don't splash. I'm Ivy. I keep the pools, and the pools are going cold.
Two degrees down since the first snow. Everyone says it's the weather.
It isn't. It's the stone dam on the low pool. Somebody's been knocking stones out of it.

speaker: ivy
lines: Whoever comes off the otter slide too fast. I'm not naming anyone.
Every slider who hits the dam takes a stone with them, and the warm water goes out the gap.
Eleven winters I've kept these pools. I'm not losing them to somebody's fun.

speaker: ivy
lines: Put the stones back in the dam. They're lying where they landed.
Then get the temperature off Corm, the raven by the steam. The glass is on his rock.
He's sat beside it a whole year and never once read it. Make him read it.
I want a number. Not news.

speaker: ivy
lines: The dam first. The stones are scattered round the low pool.
Then Corm, on his rock by the steam. Make him read the glass.
A number, mind. Not something he heard.

speaker: ivy
lines: Forty-one. Off the glass? Corm actually read it?
That's up on last week. The dam's holding. Listen to that steam.
Here. A warm stone from the bottom of the pool. Keep it in a pocket.
And if you see my sister, don't tell her I was worried.

speaker: ivy
lines: From Ilsa, my sister? She sent it with you instead of coming.
Don't say we don't look alike. Everyone says it.
She'd carry the whole valley before she'd knock on my door. Dried apples. Her good scarf.
Tell her it landed. And to come down herself next time. I'll feed her.

speaker: ivy
lines: Which house is blue? From down here, the one with the green door.
At dusk the steam turns everything up the hill blue. That one most.
Pell, the postmaster, should come down and look. He never comes down.

speaker: ivy
lines: Forty-one and holding. The dam's doing its job.
If you see my sister in the pines, say the pools are warm. Don't say I said it.
Soak your feet before you go. Everyone's feet are cold this time of year.

speaker: corm
lines: News! You'll want the news. I'm Corm. I hear it all, and I pass it on.
Word is the bakery in Hollowpine Hamlet is shut. Also, word is it's open.
Word is the post's stopped. Also, it's running. I've been saying all four since breakfast.

speaker: corm
lines: No idea! That's the trouble. I say what I hear, and I hear everything.
Just once I'd like to say a thing and have it be true.

speaker: corm
lines: Checked? I'd have to go and ask. People look at you funny when you ask.
Hearing's easier. Hearing comes to you.

speaker: corm
lines: Orla, who runs the bakery, would know if it's open.
Pell, the postmaster, would know if the post's running.
Ask them for me? Then come back and give it to me straight. I'll pass it on right, for once.

speaker: corm
lines: Back? With news? No? Orla first, at the bakery. Is it open?
Then Pell, the postmaster. Is the post running?
Then me. Slowly. I want to get it right.

speaker: corm
lines: Orla, at the bakery: is it open? Pell, the postmaster: is the post running? Then back to me.

speaker: corm
lines: The bakery's open. Post runs inside the valley. Nothing goes over the pass.
And all of it true? Checked? By somebody who asked?
Well. I'll pass that on, every word. I could get used to this.
Here, for your trouble. That's not hearsay. That's bells.

speaker: corm
lines: The pool temperature? I heard it was freezing. Jory, the mouse, told me so.
Ivy wants a reading? Off the glass? Not what I heard?
Fine. The glass is right here. I've never once read it. ...Forty-one.
Tell her forty-one. First thing I've ever checked. It felt strange.

speaker: corm
lines: I've checked things this week. Actual things. It's exhausting.
The bakery's open. The post runs inside the valley. Both true. Somebody asked.
Bring me anything you hear. I'll check it. Probably.

speaker: jory
lines: I have lived at Kettle Springs my whole life. I have never been cold.
The warm pool keeps the chill off. That is the whole reason I stay.
The pines are not far. I have heard they are not far.
I would like to go as far as the pines. Once. And come back.

speaker: jory
lines: The pines are where the cold starts. Everyone says so.
I have never felt it. I think I would like to know.
Or maybe I would not. I am not sure. Would you go first?

speaker: jory
lines: Then catch me a fish from the warm pool first. For the walk, when I go. A mouse takes lunch.
Then walk to Pinewind Wood for me. Go first, and look at it properly.
Come back and tell me what it is like. Then I will decide.

speaker: jory
lines: You are still going? Good. I am still here. I have not moved.
A fish from the warm pool first. Then the pines, in Pinewind Wood.
Then tell me what they are like. All of it. The cold too.

speaker: jory
lines: The pines are like that? Tall, and creaking, and the snow is quiet?
And it was cold, but you came back. You are standing right here.
Then I think I can go. Not today. Tomorrow. As far as the pines.
Here. For going first. I am not good at thank you.

speaker: jory
lines: I put one foot out of the warm pool this morning. Then both.
It was cold. I stood and counted to forty. Then I got back in.
Tomorrow I will count to fifty. Then the pines. You will see.

speaker: tuck
lines: Careful on the planks. I'm Tuck. I keep this bridge.
I tie it, I tighten it, I check it every hour. I don't cross it. Different job.
The rope's going. See the fraying there? Another storm and it parts.

speaker: tuck
lines: Hold on. Is that Bram's good rope? From the woodstore by the big pine?
He sent it up? With you? He hasn't said a word to me in years.

speaker: tuck
lines: Somebody has to stand at this end and watch the knots hold. That's me.
Sable, the fox at the wind post, says I'm scared. Sable files reports. I tie knots.
We'll leave it there.

speaker: tuck
lines: Forty feet, no splices. He measured it before he gave it you, didn't he.
There. Tied, tightened, tested. It'll hold a storm.
I didn't cross it. I didn't need to.
Here. I found this tied into the old rope years back. Never knew what it opens.

speaker: tuck
lines: Nettle Chimney is climbable? The tall face past the bridge? You went up it?
Then there's a way up this ridge that isn't a bridge.
I've never said I wouldn't climb. Only that I wouldn't cross.
Tell Sable I'm thinking about it. Just thinking.

speaker: tuck
lines: I check this bridge every hour. I don't cross it. Different job.
Wind's up. Rope doesn't mind wind. It minds age.
Mind the planks on your way over. I mean that kindly.

speaker: sable
lines: Sable, wind post, Windscar Ridge. I measure the wind and file a report, whatever it says.
Today's report so far reads 'windy'. That won't do.
I need two readings: one high, one low. The kite gets me the high one, over the crest.
The lantern ascent gets me the low one. I read the wind off the flames as you pass them.

speaker: sable
lines: A report that only files the good days is a lie with a stamp on it.
Tuck, the marten at the bridge, says the wind will take his bridge one day. I say the rope will.
One of us will be right. I'll file it either way.

speaker: sable
lines: The kite goes first. Get it up off the crest, above the ridge line.
Then run the lantern ascent, gate to gate. I'll watch the flames from here.
Then come back, and I'll write it up.

speaker: sable
lines: The report's still blank. Kite above the crest, please.
Then the lantern ascent, up the ridge. Then back to me.

speaker: sable
lines: Kite reading: forty, gusting. Lantern reading: the same, lower down. Consistent.
That's a report worth filing. I'll stamp it twice.
For the record, the bridge stood through all of it. Don't tell Tuck I wrote that.
Here. For the readings.

speaker: sable
lines: I've a new question. It's been on my desk a year.
Nettle Chimney is the tall face on this ridge. Nobody's tried it. I want it on the record.
Take the chimney scramble to the top. Then tell Tuck the face is climbable.
He won't cross a bridge. He's never said a word about climbing. Then come and tell me.

speaker: sable
lines: The chimney's still not on the record. Take the scramble to the top.
Then Tuck. Then me. I'll file it either way.

speaker: sable
lines: Climbable. Witnessed. I'll file it.
And Tuck's thinking about it? Tuck's never thought about anything but knots.
Two ways up this ridge now. One for crossers. One for climbers.
Here. For the climb. I'll race you up it next time.

speaker: sable
lines: Forty, gusting. Filed. I file everything.
Somebody keeps lighting the lanterns on the ridge. Good. I like a flicker.
Mind the crest. The wind doesn't file reports. It just pushes.
